description: Issue #839: at RUN TIME a profile keyword is a built-in name unconditionally. Whether a name may be DECLARED is fixed by the language version, never by the profile set: `spec/grammar.md:408` says "a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner", so the declaration-slot guard must not be gated on a profile — measured, `define ask` raises `ol-reserved-word` under a Core-Language-only set exactly as it does under this fixture's set, and the Core-only side is pinned by `core-language/check/reserved-word-profile-names-under-core-alone`. So `define ask` halts at phase-1 registration with `ol-reserved-word` and the `ask` call on line 4 never runs. A corpus that checks a rule at one stage does not cover it at the other — keep an executing case for any rule both stages implement. `check()` and `execute()` reach that answer through one predicate, `@openlogo/parser`'s `isBuiltInName`, rather than composing it each. `packages/parser/src/built-in-names.test.mjs` pins that predicate's registry coverage but does not itself drive `check()`; `packages/parser/src/checker-reserved-word.test.mjs` does, and the observable check-side case is the Core-only fixture named above. A run DOES have a profile set of its own: it is caller-supplied through `ExecuteOptions.profiles` and governs both the check and the run (`spec/execution-model.md:673-680`), defaulting to `RUN_PROFILES` — every profile this implementation supports — when the caller names none, which is this fixture's case. Both diagnostics below are therefore produced under that default, and are identical for every value of the `profiles` array above (measured through the harness's `produce()`, including empty): that array selects which DAG subsets this fixture runs in, and is not the run's claimed set (`scripts/harness/index.mjs:655-665`). The two diagnostics differ in how they depend on a claimed set: `ol-reserved-word` is raised under a Core-Language-only set too, while the line-4 `ol-bad-token` is not — measured by naming those sets through `executeOptions.profiles`, the field that does reach the run. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What a runtime copy uniquely contributes elsewhere is that the run STOPS at the fault, written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics — but `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs:68-70` deliberately excludes `ol-reserved-word` from its corpus as registration-phase, "the whole program is refused before any statement runs, so there is no partial run to truncate". The halt IS observable and IS pinned, just not there and not by this fixture: `packages/runtime/src/educational-meta-commands.test.mjs:186-204` runs a reserved-name declaration under `runUnchecked` and asserts the whole event stream is empty. Measured here the same way, `define ask … end` + `print 2` under `runUnchecked` emits 0 events where the same program with an ordinary name emits 3. This fixture does not isolate that copy, because it is checked and the check's diagnostic is the one delivered. See issue #1156 for the superseded rationale. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
